pillar_reactions.evidence: Only a one-line version of the pillar was delivered — 'the beauty about kettlebells, too, is like, it's really just turning you into an athlete, right? Because we're doing the conditioning, we're doing the strength training, we're doing the mobility, we're doing everything all at once' — but the prospect had already sold himself on it unprompted and tied it to his own goals: 'I just identify with the kettlebell actually a lot', 'I like the movements, like how it's so functional', and 'when Trevor in the video said, like, you do it, like, from your home... that actually had an immediate appeal because it breaks down the barrier.'

Diet was diagnosed ('What's your diet look like?', eat-out frequency) but the nutrition pillar was never delivered. The rep gestured at it once — 'get you on a decent diet, you know, something that's sustainable' — then immediately turned it back into a question.

Never delivered. The prospect pre-empted it himself — 'if that's one-on-one to keep me accountable, then maybe that is one-on-one' and 'to see, get actual feedback would be pretty cool' — and the rep did not build on it. Whole presentation deferred to the second call.

anchors.raw: you signed up for Primal University, now you're contemplating potentially jumping in with Trevor and doing one-on-one
anchors.note: In-house anchor, not a competitor. He bought the cheap self-serve product two days ago and has not yet opened it or bought a kettlebell — 'No, I was full. First off, I was just kind of curious as to like, since I don't have a kettlebell.' Any one-on-one price now has to be justified against content he already owns and has not used, and the rep never established what Primal University cost him or why it wouldn't be enough.

anchors.raw: I don't actually think one-on-one would be something that I would do, like, super long-term. It would just be a couple months to get the motions down.
anchors.note: He has scoped the engagement in his own head at roughly two months of form correction, against a 6- or 12-month offer. Volunteered at 00:35 and never addressed. This is the single largest unhandled risk going into the second call.

anchors.raw: the great thing about Kettleball is it doesn't take that much time, so it's, like, pretty low on the... the amount of time that you have to invest to get good results
anchors.note: He values the modality on efficiency and minimalism ('I do think there's a certain beauty in, like, as much minimalism as possible'), and has already substituted calisthenics and free sport for structured training. A low-effort, low-cost framing of the product is the frame he arrives with.

unmet_demand.want: A short engagement — roughly a couple of months of one-on-one coaching to learn correct kettlebell technique, after which he self-manages using the methodology
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is sold in 6-month and 12-month terms only; there is no two-month technique-onboarding tier

unmet_demand.want: Guidance on which product he should actually be in — he explicitly asked to be placed rather than sold: 'I ultimately kind of want to be on the best program for whatever you think my needs are'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep did not answer it on this call; he deferred to the second call and pre-framed the premium option as the answer ('I think it's like literally the perfect fit for you, dude') before any recommendation logic was shared

unmet_demand.want: Help understanding whether his hypothyroidism and his reduced sleep are limiting his results, and whether training could let him reduce his thyroid medication
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is a clinical question the programme cannot and should not answer; the rep responded with a mind-body framing rather than routing it to his physician
